title: ready-08: what heca-pro's rooms dock needs — session projects and a public FolderLine
summary: Generic heca pieces heca-pro T015 (rooms dock) waits on: a typed session→project read for services, and FolderLine on the public surface.
description:
Requested by heca-pro (session heca-pro-dev, for heca-pro T015, its rooms dock) on 2026-11-19, checked against heca 50ba6d7 and re-checked on c8206ffe. Antonio approved 2026-11-19: do it now, before P110(F010)/T567, to unblock heca-pro. Nothing here is heca-pro specific; every piece is for any extension.

Constraint: decision 15ec67fc (heca's public surface used by heca-pro stays compatible; add beside, never break) and decision 05a2ed0c (THE SYNTAX: declarative, nested builders).

Scope:
1. A service can read which project (folder) a session belongs to, and the live sessions with their project — typed, on the service contexts (heca/src/entry/service/cx.rs: StartCx/ServiceCx/ActionCx/ProjectCx), instead of submitting `list_sessions` and parsing its text. Source of truth: heca/src/server/sessions/mod.rs `SessionInfo { id, name, folder, status, … }` (crate-private today).
2. `FolderLine` (heca/src/components/folder_line.rs, `pub(crate)`; `mod components` is private in heca/src/lib.rs:10) moves to heca's public surface — heca-pro is its second caller, and by heca's rule the second caller is the move, never a copy.

Not here: the first-run region of an extension dock from config — added to P045(F006)/T528 (dock placement saved across runs), which heca-pro also waits on.

tasks.title: Services read a session's project and the sessions of a project; FolderLine becomes public
tasks.description:
For heca-pro T015 (rooms dock): it shows, in one window, the rooms of every session open on the same project, and a member's working folder the way heca shows it. Antonio approved 2026-11-19, before T567. Compatibility: decision 15ec67fc (add, never break); shape: decision 05a2ed0c (THE SYNTAX).

## 1. A session's project, read by a service
Today: the service contexts in heca/src/entry/service/cx.rs give only the session — `ActionCx::session()/session_key()` (~139-210), `ProjectCx::session()/session_key()` (~208-250); `ServiceCx` (~85) and `StartCx` (~33) give neither. The only way to learn a session's folder or the other live sessions is to `submit` `list_sessions` (heca/src/input/build/session.rs:8, heca/src/server/sessions/mod.rs:143 `SessionCommand::List`) and parse its text — every extension would repeat that parser.
Source of truth: `SessionInfo { id, name, folder: Option<PathBuf>, label, status, windows, agents }` (heca/src/server/sessions/mod.rs:13-22, pub(crate)); contexts are built in heca/src/server/services/running.rs (~121 ServiceCx, ~170 ActionCx, ~210 ProjectCx) and heca/src/server/services/mod.rs:245 (ProjectCx).
Wanted: one typed read reachable from every context that knows a session, answering (a) the project folder of a session (by `SessionKey`; `None` when it has no folder), (b) the live sessions — key, name, folder, status — so a service can group the sessions of one project. One public read type, built from the server's session list in ONE place and handed to the contexts by reference — no per-context copy of the lookup. Folder equality: compare canonical paths (same project reached through a symlink or a trailing slash is the same project). A terminated session is listed with its status, not hidden (the caller decides). Keyed by `SessionKey` (stable for the session's life), never the per-run number.
Also: when sessions change (create, rename, folder, terminate, delete), a service that shows them must be able to republish — check whether services already hear session changes; if not, say so to Antonio before adding an event.
Tests: a service reads its own session's folder; two sessions on one folder (one via a symlink) group together; a terminated session reports its status; a session with no folder reads None.

## 2. FolderLine on the public surface
Today: heca/src/components/folder_line.rs (164 lines) is `pub(crate)`, built as a struct literal `FolderLine { path, show, size, indent, theme }.build()` returning `BuiltFolderLine { widget, text: Signal<String>, visible: Signal<bool> }`; callers: the sidebar pane row and the exposé pane card. `mod components` is private (heca/src/lib.rs:10); public re-exports sit at lib.rs:30-50.
Wanted: heca-pro can write `FolderLine` and get the same line heca draws. Public form in THE SYNTAX — a constructor and typed builders (path, show, size, indent), the theme read the way other public components get it, signals readable from the built line — and the two in-crate callers move to that same form (one path, never two). Export from lib.rs next to the other public components. Rustdoc complete with a native example; docs/extending-heca.md gains the entry. Ask Antonio before changing the shape in any way the current callers would notice.

## Done when
Both reachable from a crate outside heca (an example or test in heca/examples or tests that uses only the public API), lint-changed clean, tests green, heca-pro told the API (session heca-pro-dev).

tasks.title: A child list bound to a value: a dock built from a service's data stays current
tasks.description:
Asked by heca-pro (session heca-pro-dev, 2026-11-19) for its rooms dock (heca-pro T015); Antonio decided 2026-11-19: build the DEFINITIVE fix (a declarative child list bound to a value), not a dock-rebuild stopgap; after the pending work (T568 merged, planner committed). heca-pro waits on it and adds no workaround.

## The defect (verified 2026-11-19)
A dock body that reads a reactive value while it is built never updates when the value changes. heca-pro's dock reads its `ServiceState` (from `ServiceRegistration::client(..)`, heca/src/entry/service/client.rs:19-45, a `Signal<C>`) inside `ContainerContribution::new(self, |ctx, build| state.with(|view| body(view)))`. The retained chrome tree is rebuilt only when `chrome_signature` changes (heca/src/chrome/window/retained.rs:38 — window size, font zoom, sidebar widths, pane lines, the workspace tree); a `ServiceState` change is not in it, so a new room or member shows only after a restart. docs/extending-heca.md:355 promises "In a component: it redraws when the value changes" — true for a widget bound to a signal (a label's text), false for a body whose STRUCTURE comes from the value (a list of rooms). Today every extension dock showing service data would have to wrap its body in `Keyed` plus an effect by hand — a rule each author must remember.

## Wanted — the definitive shape
A widget in heca-grid-ui that renders a collection held in a signal and keeps its children in step when the collection changes: added items get a child, removed ones lose theirs, unchanged ones keep their widget (and its focus, hover, scroll, inner state), reordered ones move — keyed by an identity the caller gives per item. In THE SYNTAX, e.g. (name and exact builders to be agreed with Antonio BEFORE code):
```rust
List::new(rooms_signal)                       // Signal<Vec<T>> or anything readable as a list (ServiceState included)
    .key(|room| room.id.clone())              // identity per item
    .child(|room| RoomRow::new(room))         // how one item is shown
```
- Builds on what exists, no second mechanism: `Keyed` / `IdentityExt::on_props` (heca-grid-ui/src/builders/identity.rs:30, props/mod.rs) and `reconcile_keyed` (heca-grid-ui/src/reconcile.rs:66). Check whether one of them already is most of this.
- Placed like any widget, in any tree (a dock body, an overlay, a pane) — a component owns its own input; nothing registered with the host.
- `ServiceState<C>` is readable by it directly (a projection `|view| &view.rooms`), so an extension writes no glue.
- Decision 05a2ed0c names this gap ("A declarative child list bound to data (ForEach-like) is not in the library yet"); P087(F011)/T469 (the palette rewrite) consumes the same widget — design it for both.
- Plugins: a ViewNode cannot carry a signal (AGENTS ⭐ SETTLED); the plugin-side counterpart is P085(F003)/T360 (per-mount values). Say how the two meet; do not build T360 here.
- Fix docs/extending-heca.md:355 to show the real way (the list widget), plus the widget's rustdoc, docs/widgets.md entry (native example) and the showcase.

## Tests
Headless: change the signal → children added/removed/reordered with unchanged ones keeping their widget identity (a child's own state survives); a dock built once with the widget updates without a chrome rebuild; break the reconcile on purpose and see the tests go red. Eye-check: heca-pro's rooms dock adds a room live.

- Children that follow a value through the one door for children: `.child(rooms.map(RoomRow::new))` (MapChildren on a Signal<Vec<T>>), `.child(shown.map(|view| &view.rooms, RoomRow::new))` (ServiceState::map, heca/src/entry/service/client.rs). General form BoundChildren::new(read, make) (heca-grid-ui/src/builders/bound.rs). IntoChildren gained `attach` (children.rs); Parent::child goes through it. Base holds the ranges (`bound`), counts a changed value in needs_layout, and the layout pass puts them in step before reading the node (layout/build.rs). An item is its own identity; unchanged children are kept (focus/state), new made, gone dropped, moved moved; children sit directly in the container between those written around them; the frame after the change shows it. One generic matcher reconcile_matching (heca-grid-ui/src/reconcile.rs) serves this and the existing reconcile.

tasks.title: A program's agent icon, read by name — extensions draw the harness icon heca draws
tasks.description:
Asked by heca-pro (heca-pro-dev, 2026-11-19) for its rooms dock (heca-pro T015): each member is shown with its harness icon, drawn with heca's Image widget like heca's agent line does. Antonio chose option (a) on 2026-11-19: a public read "program → icon of the registered driver" (plugin/extension drivers included), so no extension copies heca's SVGs. API name to be agreed with Antonio before code.

## What exists (verified 2026-11-19)
- `heca::agent::AgentIcon` is public (heca-core/src/agent/icon.rs:9: File(PathBuf) | Svg(String)); re-exported in heca/src/agent/mod.rs:11-14.
- Every driver implements `heca::agent::AgentDriver` (heca-core/src/agent/driver.rs:44-60): `id()` (stable identity, e.g. "claude", the key of `[settings.agents.programs.<id>]`), `name()`, `icon() -> Option<AgentIcon>`, `programs()` (executable names), `recognizes(program)` (basename match, `program_name`, driver.rs:99).
- Built-in drivers live in heca/src/agent/drivers/ (private; assets in drivers/assets/icons: claude, codex, pi, opencode); extensions add drivers with `heca::extension(..).agent_driver(..)` (heca/src/agent/registration/).
- There is NO public lookup from a program to its icon; an extension sees PaneFacts (with the running agent's state/icon) only inside pane_line/pane_chip.
- CAVEAT: a built-in driver is constructed only when its program is enabled in config (`configured()` returns None unless `enabled: Some(true)`, heca/src/agent/drivers/mod.rs:33-36), and config.default.toml ships every program disabled (`[settings.agents.programs.*] enabled = false`). A lookup over the live driver list would find no icon for a program whose integration is off. The icon is static data: the lookup must answer for every known driver, enabled or not — decide with Antonio how (e.g. the icons registered beside the drivers regardless of enablement).
- Naming of the key: heca-pro says "claude-code"; heca's driver id is "claude" and its executable "claude". The lookup should accept what heca already uses (driver id or an executable the driver recognizes); heca-pro passes one of those.

## Wanted
One public read in heca::agent: program (driver id or executable) → the icon heca would draw (driver's icon; for an unknown program, None, and the caller shows heca's generic terminal glyph as the agent line does). Built once, from the same registry the agent line uses — no second list. Docs in docs/extending-heca.md (Terminal agent drivers section); a test from outside the crate (heca/tests) that reads a built-in driver's icon with its integration disabled and an extension driver's icon.
tasks.notes: Decided with Antonio 2026-11-19: (1) the key is the DRIVER ID ("claude", "codex", "pi", "opencode", an extension driver's id) — not the executable: a driver can have several executables, the user changes them in config (`executables = [...]`), while the id is unique, stable and the config key. (2) The icon does not depend on whether the driver's integration is enabled: it is returned for every known driver, enabled or not. API name still to agree before code.

Implement the read over the one driver registry, enabled or not; tests incl. outside-crate
Docs (extending-heca.md); tell heca-pro the API; PR

tasks.title: The pane card look as a Row variant; no hand-written styling left in the app
tasks.description:
Antonio approved 2026-11-19 (heca-pro's first request + the cleanup he asked for after I failed to flag it). Rule (AGENTS § 0 / the six component steps): components are built with Grid (several parts) or Flex (like things) from small widgets; nothing written by hand at a call site — no background, alpha, radius, padding, colour or pixel number; a look two places need is a variant/builder in heca-grid-ui.

## 1. The card look as a Row variant (heca-pro needs it for its member card)
heca/src/providers/workspaces/pane_row.rs:178-185 writes the card by hand: `Row::new().background(theme.colors.foreground.with_alpha(alpha_u8(theme.colors.card_background_alpha))).radius(theme.colors.control_radius()).padding(Spacing::Sm)`. The exposé card (heca/src/chrome/surfaces/expose/pane_card.rs:116-118) writes its own: `.background(theme.colors.surface).radius(theme.colors.control_radius()).padding(Spacing::Xs)` (its comment explains why the map card is a surface, not a wash — two looks, both named, both in the library). One variant/builder on Row that owns each look from the theme (name agreed with Antonio before code); pane row, exposé card and heca-pro use it; public, documented in docs/widgets.md with the showcase.

## 2. pane_row.rs, everything that breaks the rules (found 2026-11-19)
- the hand-written card look (above);
- hand-picked colours: `Icon::new(info.icon).color(theme.colors.foreground)` (:93), the `(program)` suffix `.color(theme.colors.foreground)` (:131) — colour from the theme through the widget/variant, not at the call site;
- hand-sent events on click: two `emit.fire(..)` (FocusDock + CursorTo, ~:205-220) — one of the 13 sites owned by P087(F011)/T565; coordinate, do not duplicate;
